description: The HR analytics team has accumulated 12,000 employee performance reviews in the PERF_REVIEWS table (owned by HR schema), all with STATUS='NEW'. These must be batch-processed nightly by a production-grade PL/SQL ETL pipeline that avoids row-by-row processing overhead. Using Oracle SQL Developer connected to the HR schema (hr/hr123): (1) Create a PL/SQL package named HR.REVIEW_ETL_PKG with a complete package specification and package body. The package body must implement a procedure PROCESS_REVIEWS that uses BULK COLLECT with a LIMIT clause to retrieve and process rows in batches — for each batch, compute a NORMALIZED_SCORE as ROUND((raw_score / max_possible_score) * 100, 2), update STATUS to 'PROCESSED', and write a summary entry to the ETL_RUN_LOG table using an autonomous transaction sub-procedure named LOG_ETL_RUN (declared with PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION). The package should also declare a weakly-typed REF CURSOR type and a function GET_UNPROCESSED that returns a REF CURSOR over unprocessed reviews. (2) Execute REVIEW_ETL_PKG.PROCESS_REVIEWS to process all 12,000 rows. (3) Create a view HR.VW_REVIEW_SUMMARY that joins PERF_REVIEWS with the DEPARTMENTS table and aggregates processed reviews by department: showing department_name, review_count, average normalized_score, and the reviewer_id with the highest review count. (4) Export the view contents to /home/ga/Documents/exports/review_summary.csv. System credentials if needed: system/OraclePassword123.
